title: TrES-2b - The Darkest Planet Ever Found

target.note: v2 spec: short declaratives, simple words, one idea per beat. Read-aloud simple.

narration:
Look at this planet. You will never see it. Not once, not ever.
It bounces back less than one percent of the light its star sends down.
That is darker than coal. Darker than asphalt. The instruments checked it twice. Both times they agreed.
Here is the part that makes this darkness obscene. The planet is tidally locked. One side never moves.
One half faces the star forever. The other half never sees it at all.
So the night side never warms. The day side never cools.
That day side is a furnace. Thousands of degrees of gas.
It does glow, faintly. A dull red. About two thousand kelvin. Like coals left in a hearth.
Hot enough to strip the skin off your hand. Too dark to reflect the light that made it hot.
Now watch the star it orbits. The star is what finishes this story.
The star is small and red. It is running low on the fuel that keeps it alive.
So it is swelling. It is creeping closer. It is pulling the air off the planet.
The whole atmosphere comes off in sheets, trailing away as a long glowing tail.
And the darkest planet anyone has ever found is being unmade by its own sun.
